sections.h2: Who sends a property tax bill to a Johnson City homeowner?
sections.html:
Two bills can arrive. The city's Finance Department sends the city bill and takes the city payment, while the Washington County Trustee takes in the county tax on the same parcel. The city's property tax page gives the Municipal and Safety Building, 601 E. Main St., as the walk-in counter, staffed on weekdays from eight in the morning until five. Checks can go by post to Box 2227, Johnson City, TN 37605, and anyone with a late balance can reach the tax office at 423-434-6299.

The county side runs through two other offices. The Assessor of Property at 423-753-1671 handles appraisal and mailing address questions, while the Trustee at 423-753-1602 only collects. The Trustee's county tax page says plainly that it does not appraise property or set the rate.

Johnson City sits mostly in Washington County, with smaller pieces in Carter and Sullivan counties. A parcel in either of those slivers answers to that county's assessor and trustee, so read the county off your parcel record before dialing.

sections.h2: When is Johnson City property tax due this year?
sections.html:
The city says 2026 notices went out the week of October 12, and payment is due by February 28, 2027. The city will honor a postmark from that day or earlier, and penalty and interest begin accruing March 1, 2027. The county notice follows a similar track: the Trustee mails in October, takes payment through the end of February, and adds 1.5% interest to unpaid balances on March 1.

The county page picks November 15 as its cutoff for a missing notice, and that date is today: any owner still waiting on a county bill should contact the Trustee right now. Tennessee owners are expected to pay whether or not a notice arrives. A homeowner whose lender pays from escrow will not receive a bill, so ask the servicer for proof of payment.

Ways to pay the city portion:

  • In person at 601 E. Main St. during weekday hours
  • By mail to the P.O. Box above
  • Online through the Finance Department's payment system, which adds a 2.75% processing fee per transaction

The city notes that online accounts past the due date are delinquent and cannot be paid online, and neither can taxes already filed in Chancery Court. For those balances call 423-434-6299 to confirm the exact payoff before sending money.

sections.h2: What kind of city is Johnson City, and how does that shape a sale?
sections.html:
Johnson City began in 1856 as a railroad stop called Johnson's Depot and was incorporated in 1869. Three rail lines crossed downtown at the peak, and the city later grew around East Tennessee State University, Ballad Health and the medical campus that includes Johnson City Medical Center and the VA hospital at Mountain Home. It sits in an Appalachian valley near Boone Lake on the Watauga River, and Buffalo Mountain, a ridge above 2,700 feet, is a city park on the south side.

Weather is a fact of life for older houses here. Rainfall averages about 45 inches a year and snow roughly 16 inches, which keeps roofs, gutters and crawl spaces working through damp summers and cold, wet winters. Most of the Washington County side is served by Johnson City Schools, whose campuses include Science Hill High School and University School, while a few edges fall under the county districts.

Census Bureau QuickFacts gives a picture of the housing stock:

  • A July 2025 estimate of 74,943 people, which is 5.5% above the 2020 base
  • 51.3% of homes lived in by their owners, leaving roughly half to renters
  • $268,200 as the typical value of an owner's home in the 2020 to 2024 survey
  • Rent near $1,023 a month and household income near $57,254
  • 20.3% of residents below the poverty line

With roughly half the households renting, a Johnson City seller may be a landlord with tenants in place, and the city and county balances for that rental should be pulled before an offer is signed.

sections.h2: How is the Johnson City tax amount figured?
sections.html:
Residential property is assessed at 25% of appraised value, and the rate is charged per $100 of that assessment. The Washington County Trustee's page walks through a $150,000 home: $37,500 of assessment multiplied by the county rate, with the final bill trimmed to whole dollars since tax year 2020. Its table lists a county rate of $2.15 per $100 under the heading 2023, so treat that number as dated and read the rate off your own 2026 notice.

The city adds its own rate on top for houses inside Johnson City limits. The city's page leaves the rate out, so City Finance is the place to get today's figure. Kingsport's own tax explainer mentions that Washington County values rose in 2024, so many owners here saw a new appraisal that year.

sections.h2: What can I do if I think my Johnson City assessment is wrong?
sections.html:
Start with the Washington County Assessor of Property at 423-753-1671. An informal review, where an assessor offers one, is only a conversation and does not count as an appeal, the Comptroller points out. The real first step is the board that hears county complaints, which sits in June, and a disputed value usually becomes final if that board is skipped.

Someone who loses at the county level can file with the state board by August 1, or 45 days after the county notice was sent if that falls later. On the state appeal page, the strongest proof for a house is a set of comparable sales with the differences explained. Saying the home is overvalued without numbers rarely works, and a jump after a countywide reappraisal is not itself proof of a mistake.

While the appeal is open, the undisputed share of the bill still has to be paid before it goes delinquent, along with any back taxes from earlier years.

sections.h2: Who pays the tax if a Johnson City house sells this winter?
sections.html:
Under the county's description, the tax roll shows whoever owned the property on January 1, so the seller often receives the bill even after a fall sale. The usual practice is to prorate at closing, after which the buyer carries the tax. The closing agent requests payoffs from the city and the Trustee and pays them out of the seller's proceeds.

When a bill is already late, get the payoff straight from the tax office, since online balances can trail payments still in transit. If the account has gone to Chancery Court, payment goes through the Clerk and Master and cannot be made on the city's website. A cash sale that closes quickly can clear those balances at the table, which helps when an inherited or tenant-occupied house has fallen behind.

faqs.q: When does the 2026 Johnson City tax bill go late?
faqs.a: Right after February 28, 2027. The city treats a postmark from that day as on time and starts penalty and interest March 1, 2027, and the county Trustee also takes county payments through the end of February.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Johnson City property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes, for current balances. The city charges a 2.75% processing fee per transaction. Delinquent accounts and taxes filed in Chancery Court cannot be paid online, so call 423-434-6299 for the exact payoff.

faqs.q: What if no county tax notice ever showed up?
faqs.a: Phone the Washington County Trustee at 423-753-1602. The county wants to hear from owners who have no notice by November 15, and the tax remains owed without one.

faqs.q: Does Johnson City tax apply to houses in Carter or Sullivan County?
faqs.a: The city bills its own tax inside city limits in every county, but the county portion goes to that county's trustee. Look up the county on your parcel record and contact that county's assessor and trustee for dates and rates.

faqs.q: Can a Johnson City house with back taxes be sold?
faqs.a: Yes, a sale can go ahead. Back city and county balances come out of the seller's proceeds, and the title company needs a current payoff from the tax office to do it.
